section2: Compliance with the Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998 (PUWER) is a fundamental legal duty for employers operating storage systems throughout Suffolk. Regulations 5 and 6 mandate that all work equipment, including static pallet racking and cantilever storage, is maintained in an efficient state and inspected at suitable intervals by competent personnel. The Health and Safety Executive's HSG76 guidance document establishes the mandatory three-tier inspection hierarchy for warehouses. Tier one requires daily informal checks by warehouse staff to identify acute impact damage. Tier two demands weekly formal visual inspections conducted by a trained company Person Responsible for Racking Safety (PRRS). Tier three requires an annual comprehensive structural examination performed by an independent SEMA Approved Racking Inspector (SARI). For the shipping logisticians, agricultural processors, and retail distributors stationed across Suffolk, failing to adhere to PUWER 1998 and HSG76 carries severe legal consequences. A structural racking failure caused by neglected damage can result in fatal workplace accidents, immediate HSE prohibition notices, unlimited corporate fines, and severe personal injury liabilities for company directors.
section3: Rackstor UK Ltd executes all structural integrity audits strictly in accordance with Storage Equipment Manufacturers Association (SEMA) guidelines, utilizing the traffic light grading system. Green denotes minor surface wear or deflection well within safe manufacturing tolerances; no immediate action is required. Amber indicates significant structural deformation exceeding safe limits—such as an upright post deflection greater than 3mm front-to-back or 5mm side-to-side, or a damaged beam showing permanent set—requiring the affected bay to be offloaded or load-reduced, with professional repairs executed within 4 weeks. Red represents critical structural failure, such as a severely buckled leg, sheared anchor bolts, or fractured beam connectors, mandating an immediate-danger cordon, zero load tolerance, and urgent repair before re-loading. Clients receive a comprehensive written report itemising every defect with photographic evidence and engineering recommendations.
